evidence.curator_note: Radical-cation McLafferty-type gamma-H rearrangement (labelled rH) of an ALPHA,BETA-unsaturated carbonyl molecular ion (the drawn C=C is conjugated to the C=O; the migrating gamma-H sits on the R-CH2 gamma carbon) through a 6-membered cyclic transition state, giving a conjugated dienol radical cation. Book draws 5 single-barb (fishhook) arcs (zoomed re-read): (i) the O odd-electron reaching toward the migrating gamma-H (arrowhead points left toward the H), (ii) the gamma C-H bond fishhook (the C-H bond breaks, the H leaving as an atom toward O), (iii) formation of the C3=C5 pi bond, (iv) the C5=C6 -> C6=C7 shift, and (v) the carbonyl pi (C7=O) rotating up onto O. Only the two heavy-atom framework pi-pair shifts that the arrow gate can track are emitted as electron_moves: C7=O -> C6=C7 (move 1) and C5=C6 -> C3=C5 (move 2), drawn by the book as single-barb fishhooks but encoded as two double-barbed pair shifts. The gamma-H migration from C3 to O and the O-radical's role in abstracting it are carried IMPLICITLY by the heavy-atom hydrogen counts (RDKit absorbs an explicit mapped H, so a C-H -> O-H bond move cannot be tracked in this schema); the odd electron remains on oxygen (O+.) across the step, consistent with the MOD rule DFS.

Vinylogous radical-site alpha-cleavage (labelled a) of the dienol ion: the odd electron relays from O through the conjugated system to expel R. at the far end, giving the resonance-stabilized even-electron oxocarbenium C6H9O+ (charge delocalized over O and the diene; the O+-localized Kekule form is drawn/encoded here). Book draws 5 single-barb (fishhook) arcs: R. departure (arc pointing back onto R), C2=C3 formation, the internal C3=C5 -> C5=C6 shift, C6=C7 -> C7=O, and the O odd-electron into the new C=O. These are the seven single-electron moves' drawn subset (moves 1,2,4,6,7); the two pair-completing hooks (moves 3 and 5: C3=C5 -> C2=C3 and C6=C7 -> C5=C6) are NOT drawn on the page and are added here for electron balance. The odd electron ends on the departing R (R. radical), so oxygen carries no radical in the product ion.

Cross-linked MOD rules (rule_index by_equation 8.9): rH step <-> IMS_8_9_1_CH3 / IMS_8_9_1_OCH3 ("stabil Dienol Ion 8.9 row 1 process 1 rH"); alpha step <-> IMS_8_9_2_CH3 / IMS_8_9_2_OCH3 ("row 1 process 2 alpha"). VERIFIED at the connectivity level: the IMS_8_9_1 DFS moves H (map 4 in the rule) from the gamma-carbon to O with C3=C5 and C6=C7 formation and C5=C6/C7=O loss (matches step_rH), and IMS_8_9_2 forms C2=C3, C4=C5 and C6=O while ejecting R (matches step_alpha). MISMATCH (see rule_mismatches): the IMS_8_9_2 PRODUCT DFS keeps a radical dot on oxygen ([O+.]) while the same O also carries a C=O double bond and an O-H (over-valent) AND marks the departing R as a radical ([_A.]1) -> two unpaired electrons out of a one-radical precursor (spin non-conservation); the conservation guardrail would drop this rule. The chemically correct product ion is the even-electron oxocarbenium [O+] encoded here (odd electron fully relayed to R). m/z values (M+. 112.0883; product 97.0648) are computed from the curator's instantiation (R = CH3, X = CH3; the scheme is generic in R and X = CH3/OCH3) and are not printed in the book.
